title: Allan's Dam and Macdonell bridge environmental assessment approved
subtitle: Also: Baker Library 40-year lease, KPMG as auditor, utility billing by-law, back-office review, Elect Respect pledge.
overview: Council approved the Macdonell and Allan's Structures Environmental Assessment {{vote:m14}} and directed staff to issue the Notice of Completion. The preferred option rehabilitates Allan's dam rather than removing it. Delegates asked for a hydraulic study of removal, and two amendments to explore it or to require an information report both failed {{vote:m12}} {{vote:m13}}. Staff said they would return to Council if detailed design finds the rehabilitation is not feasible.

Council also approved a lease for the Baker Library facility. Council changed the term from 30 years with two five-year renewals to 40 years with one ten-year renewal {{vote:m9}}. On the consent report, Council appointed KPMG LLP as external auditor for 2025 through 2029, approved commemorative names including Brooklyn Park, and set Q1 2026 for the utility billing by-law {{vote:m6}}.

Council directed staff to fold back-office centralization recommendations into annual workplans {{vote:m10}} and endorsed the Elect Respect pledge {{vote:m17}}. After a closed session, the Mayor reported that Council gave direction to staff on a Superior Court decision update and two Ontario Land Tribunal matters. The Mayor also invited residents to a virtual 2026 budget town hall on October 30.

decisions.detail: Council approved the environmental assessment and directed staff to issue the Notice of Completion, with rehabilitation of Allan's dam as the preferred option.
Staff must salvage, retain and conserve the steel railing and salvageable superstructure of Allan's Bridge for reuse near the bridge.
Staff will work with the Arts and Culture and Heritage advisory committees on commemoration, placemaking and heritage conservation during design.
The Deputy CAO is directed to enter a lease for the Baker Library facility for 40 years with one ten-year renewal.
KPMG LLP is appointed as the City's external auditor for fiscal years 2025 through 2029.
Council received the project update, set Q1 2026 for the Customer Accounts by-law, and amended the Stormwater by-law.
Staff will incorporate the review's recommendations into the annual workplan process where appropriate.
Council endorsed the pledge, committed to six standards of respectful conduct, and will send the resolution to other governments and police services.

debate: Delegates from cycling, youth, environmental and water groups asked for a hydraulic study of removing Allan's dam before the assessment was finalized. They cited flood risk to about 80 upstream homes, algae, warm water and fish passage. A developer delegate agreed the flood model is outdated but asked that Council stay engaged during design.

Staff said an environmental assessment does not need perfect information and that detailed design will refine the hydraulic modelling. They said removal would be a large undertaking involving sediment and possible contamination, permits from several agencies, Metrolinx structures and public engagement. Some residents also want to keep the mill pond.

Several councillors called the amendment to study removal premature. They said staff would return to Council if risks emerged. A proponent of the amendment said that without it staff would scope only rehabilitation, so this was the last chance to ask for a serious look at removal.

On the information-report amendment, staff said it would add work and was unnecessary because they would bring a full report if the design deviated. A councillor also noted that voting against the staff recommendation could limit a later request to reconsider.
On the Baker Library lease, staff said they supported 40 years, since concerns about a redevelopment clause mainly applied to much longer leases.
